headline: A study by Mercor found that AI models beat licensed accountants on simplified bookkeeping tasks, but still cannot do a whole accounting job without human oversight.
score_reason: Pool score kept: the article matches the headline, but it is a short report on a single company's study of simplified tasks.
importance_line: Accountants and the firms that employ them may see routine bookkeeping sped up, but the test covered only simplified, detail-checking tasks and the findings are Mercor's own study as relayed by one outlet.
summary: The Decoder reports on a Mercor study in which 12 licensed accountants and AI models worked through simplified tasks from the APEX Accounting Benchmark; the accountants averaged about 37 percent, while the best models now solve the same tasks almost flawlessly. On the full 160-task benchmark the top model, Claude Opus 5.5, met 61.8 percent of grading criteria and no model fully solved almost 60 percent of tasks, and Mercor admits the study left out client conversations and long-built context.
notes: Study is Mercor's own; publication date of the study not stated in the article.
